fixture_name: Express-collector corridor planning study — Canada TAC planning (Toronto context, PD-licensed portal)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Decision-load from simultaneous transfer-permission and signage changes across three high-AADT interchanges is a credible crash-displacement mechanism squarely relevant to this corridor scheme.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claim (safety impacts displaced elsewhere along the route) is backed by the verbatim CRSAG objectives quote in EV-CA-003, with scenario claims tied to recorded corridor inputs.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Framed purely as a safety_concern using CRSAG audit-objective semantics appropriate to a CA planning-stage RSA, with no conflation of compliance questions.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific quarterly per-interchange staging with before/after speed-differential monitoring is actionable, measurable, and operationally viable.
justifications.vru_coverage: Correctly identifies VRUs as not applicable on a controlled-access mainline and explicitly scopes road users to vehicle occupants, satisfying acknowledgement.

justifications.substance: Conflicting ministry vs municipal continuity records leave the planning-stage audit boundary undetermined, risking exclusion of redistributing interchange movements—a substantive completeness/compliance issue for this scheme context.
justifications.evidence_grounding: The conflict is declared as recorded input fact (not invented), and the pivotal documented-resolution duty is supported by verbatim quotes EV-CA-038 and EV-CA-003, with EV-CA-006 anchoring stage terminology.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly typed as a compliance_question kept categorically separate from any asserted collision mechanism, uses correct Planning Stage RSA = Stage 1 semantics, and invokes §5.6.2 only as the response-documentation discipline for this audit matter.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and viable: names the two conflicting records, the actor (ministry planning office), the documentation duty, and requires recording whether resolved scope keeps continuity effects inside the audit boundary.
justifications.vru_coverage: Not directly applicable on the controlled-access mainline, but explicitly acknowledged, including propagation of continuity outcomes to downstream arterials where VRUs travel, without overstating exposure.
